A walk-forward nowcast of a refiner's monthly stock return from monthly refining fundamentals (crack spreads, crude
differentials, product prices, inventories, demand). Each month the model selects and calibrates its variables on past data
only, trades the residual (actual minus nowcast return), and a 3-state Markov regime filter decides when to trade with or
against the signal. With `RUN_ALL = TRUE` one render runs the main stock and every peer with the same settings and ends with a
comparison of all stocks (section 13). Data files are not included; see `data/README.md` for the expected layout.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
pkgs <- c("readxl", "openxlsx", "matrixStats", "ggplot2", "scales", "knitr")
missing_pkgs <- pkgs[!vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs)) install.packages(missing_pkgs, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
invisible(lapply(pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE))
library(parallel)
HAS_RAGG <- requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.5,
                      fig.retina = 2, dev = if (HAS_RAGG) "ragg_png" else "png")
if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("MR_CHILD_STOCK"))) knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = TRUE)   # peer run: a chart that fails (e.g. too few years) does not stop the report
```

# 1. Configuration

All settings are in this chunk. Run with `QUICK_MODE <- TRUE` first, then `FALSE` for the full run.

**How the model works (overview):**

- **Variable scores:** every candidate variable is scored monthly on significance (p-value), stability of its R² and its own out-of-sample R², each standardised over a rolling window; the weights of the three scores are calibrated.
- **Selection and nowcast:** the top-ranked variables (limited by a correlation cap `Corr_t` and `VIF_MAX`) form the nowcast for the trade month; with `COMBINE_VARS = "univariate"` the forecast averages one-variable regressions.
- **Calibration:** windows, number of variables, `Corr_t` and score weights are calibrated every month on the out-of-sample R² of past test windows (SPSA optimiser, warm start); `SMOOTH_TABLE` sets how each calibrated value is smoothed and the range it may take. With `OWN_START = TRUE` every stock first searches its own starting point, using data up to that month only.
- **Trading:** a trade opens when the residual exceeds `Min_Res` × its standard deviation; take-profit and stop-loss at 1 × |residual|, holding up to `MAX_HOLD_M` months in overlapping sleeves, 10 bps per side.
- **Validation strategies:** baseline and four variants that re-check the calibrated parameters on a later validation window ((a) choose, (b) gate, (c) both, (d) switch).
- **Markov regime filter (`MK_METHOD = "hmm3b"`):** a 3-state hidden Markov model on the stock's return deviation, the model's variance ratio and the slope of its OOS R², fitted monthly on past data only. "Flip" reverses the trade in the low state; "graded" uses an ensemble of fits (`MK_ENS_WINDOWS`). Every strategy × Markov rule is reported in one grid; `COMBINED_STRATEGY` + `COMBINED_MARKOV` is the headline model.
- **No lookahead:** every window, score, calibration and regime fit at month *t* uses data up to *t* only (checked in section 7).

```{r config}
QUICK_MODE <- TRUE   # TRUE for the first check run, then FALSE for the full run

# ---- trading ------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY_DAY     <- 0        # 0 = close of the signal month's last trading day
                          # 1 / 2 / 3 = close of the 1st / 2nd / 3rd trading day of the next month
COST_PER_SIDE <- 0.0010   # 10 bps per side, charged on changes in net exposure
MAX_HOLD_M    <- 6        # maximum holding period (months) = number of sleeves

# ---- model windows ---------------------------------------------------------------
TRAIN_WIN_STEP <- 6       # grid step of the training window (its range is in the parameter table, row Train_Win)
TEST_WIN_STEP  <- 4       # grid step of the test window (range: row Test_Win)
TRAIN_PER_VAR   <- 12     # Train_Win >= 12 x n (with COMBINE_VARS = "univariate" every regression has ONE variable, so the
                          #   12:1 rule then applies per regression and does not cap n; the n row of the table is the only cap)
TEST_PER_VAR    <- 0      # Test_Win  >= 8 x n when 8; 0 = test ratio off (the test window does not limit n)
WINDOW_SCORE_MONTHS <- 6  # screen: a window pair is scored by its OOS R2 averaged over the last 6 months
WINDOW_UPDATE <- "monthly" # "monthly" = window pair re-chosen every month; "january" = once a year (old behaviour)
WINDOW_TOP_K  <- 1         # top-K pairs from the screen get a full parameter calibration (plus the current pair);
                           # the pair with the best calibrated OOS R2 is used. 1 = screen only.
TEST_INCLUDES_TRADE_MONTH <- FALSE  # FALSE: calibration test window ends at month t-1 and month t is
                                     #        priced as the first month after it (recommended)
                                     # TRUE:  month t is the last month of the test window

# ---- trade rules (chosen after the model) -----------------------------------------
FIXED_T     <- 1.0                          # TP = 1 x |residual| (fixed, not calibrated)
FIXED_S     <- 1.0                          # SL = 1 x |residual| (fixed, not calibrated)
T_GRID      <- FIXED_T; S_GRID <- FIXED_S   # single values: the grid search below only varies Min_Res
MINRES_GRID <- seq(0.00, 0.60, by = 0.05)   # ONLY calibrated trade rule: trade if |residual| > Min_Res x SD(test residuals)
MIN_SIGNALS_FOR_TRADE_CALIB <- 6            # fewer past signals in the test window -> defaults below
DEFAULT_TRADE_RULES <- c(t = FIXED_T, s = FIXED_S, min_res = 0.0)

# ---- smoothing ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SMOOTHING <- "average"   # "average" = each parameter smoothed as set in the parameter table below; "none" = all raw
WARM_START <- TRUE   # FALSE = main start is the default point (last month's result is still added as an extra start)
OWN_START  <- TRUE   # TRUE = every stock (VLO too) finds its OWN starting parameters: at its first month with enough data, OWN_START_DRAWS
                     #   random parameter sets (anywhere in the table's ranges) plus the default are scored, and the best
                     #   OWN_START_TOP are optimised; the winner replaces the default start (Regr 36, Z 30, Train_MO 24, Test_MO 9,
                     #   n 5, Corr_t 0.7, equal weights). Uses data up to that month only, and the backtest starts at that month.
                     #   FALSE = default start for every stock.
OWN_START_DRAWS <- 40; OWN_START_TOP <- 4
                          # TRUE  = main start is last month's calibration with a narrower spread
# ---- PARAMETER TABLE: one row per parameter / window / weight. Edit it here. -----------------------------------
#   method, months = smoothing of the value used each month:
#       "none" = raw calibrated value; "ema" = exponential average (months = EMA length);
#       "mean", "median", "mode", "midrange", "midhinge" = over the last `months` raw values (Inf or NA = all history)
#   min, max      = range the calibration may choose from (NA = no limit / default):
#       Regr_Win, Z_Win, Train_MO, Test_MO, Train_Win, Test_Win in months; n = number of variables;
#       Corr_t and the weights a, d, f between 0 and 1 (weights are shares that sum to 1); Min_Res within its grid (0-0.6)
#   Every parameter, window and weight is set here and nowhere else. A calibrated parameter without a row is used raw.
#   Rows for parameters in FIXED_PARAMS (or weights not in WEIGHTS) have no effect.
SMOOTH_TABLE <- read.table(header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, text = "
  name       method   months  min   max
  Regr_Win   midrange Inf     20    100
  Z_Win      midrange Inf     20    100
  Train_MO   midrange Inf     12    100
  Test_MO    midrange Inf     6     100
  n          midrange Inf     5     8
  Corr_t     midrange Inf     0.1   1
  a          ema      18      0     1
  d          ema      18      0     1
  f          ema      18      0     1
  Min_Res    ema      18      0     0.6
  Train_Win  midrange Inf     60    120
  Test_Win   midrange Inf     24    24
")

# ---- forecast shrinkage and combination (raise OOS R2 by cutting forecast variance) --------------
# All three apply inside the nowcast itself, so calibration, validation, the Markov inputs and the trades all use them.
SHRINK <- 1   # fitted value = training mean + SHRINK x (model forecast - training mean)
                          #   1 = off (full model forecast); 0.5 = half-way to the historical mean; 0 = historical mean only
                          #   (shrinking towards the mean benchmark is what the OOS R2 rewards for over-confident forecasts)
COMBINE_VARS <- "univariate"   # "none"       = one multiple regression on the selected variables (previous behaviour)
                          # "univariate" = equal-weight average of one-variable regressions, one per selected variable
                          #                (Rapach, Strauss & Zhou 2010 combination forecast)
                          # "mix"        = half the multiple regression + half the univariate average
UNIVARIATE_FIX_N <- FALSE  # with COMBINE_VARS = "univariate", n is calibrated (removed from FIXED_PARAMS); TRUE = keep n fixed
COMBINE_TRAIN <- 0   # average the forecast over training windows within +/- COMBINE_TRAIN months of the chosen one,
                          #   on the TRAIN_WIN_STEP grid and inside TRAIN_WIN_RANGE (same variables, same test window)
                          #   0 = off; 12 = up to 5 windows (step 6); Inf = every training length in the range
                          #   (Pesaran & Pick 2011: combining across estimation windows)

# ---- data and output ----------------------------------------------------------------
MIN_OBS_FRAC <- 0.80; LOGZ_EPS <- 0.01; SEED <- 20260926
PROJECT_DIR <- local({ f <- tryCatch(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(f)) getwd() else dirname(normalizePath(f)) })                  # folder of this file
DATA_DIR  <- file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "data")      # input files (not included in the repository)
RESULTS_DIR <- file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "results") # output folders are created here
DATA_FILE <- "fundamentals_monthly.xlsx"   # monthly data: col 1 = month, col 2 = main stock's monthly return, then one column per variable
# ---- which stock -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
STOCK      <- "VLO"            # main stock of this render: "VLO" or a peer name from PEER_COLS
DAILY_FILE <- "main_stock_daily.xlsx"  # main stock's daily returns (column 1 = date, column 2 = daily return)
# Peers: daily returns of other companies in ONE file in DATA_DIR, sheet "DailyChanges": Date + one column per company.
PEER_FILE  <- "peers_daily.xlsx"
PEER_COLS  <- c(DINO = "HFSinclair", DK = "Delek", CVI = "CvrEnerg", MPC = "Marathon", PBF = "PBFEnergy", PSX = "Philips66",
                SUN = "Sunoco")   # ticker = column name in PEER_FILE; a new company = one more entry here
# ---- run all stocks in one render ---------------------------------------------------------------
RUN_ALL          <- TRUE       # TRUE = run STOCK, then every stock in RUN_ALL_STOCKS with these same settings, and add
                               #   section 13 comparing them all; FALSE = STOCK only
RUN_ALL_STOCKS   <- names(PEER_COLS)                       # peers to run, in this order; or a subset, e.g. c("DK", "CVI")
RUN_ALL_PARALLEL <- 1          # peer runs at the same time: 1 = one after another (~1 h each); 2 only on 8+ cores
CHILD <- Sys.getenv("MR_CHILD_STOCK")                       # set only inside a peer run started by RUN_ALL (do not edit)
if (nzchar(CHILD)) { STOCK <- CHILD; RUN_ALL <- FALSE }
if (STOCK %in% names(PEER_COLS)) DAILY_FILE <- PEER_FILE
Y_FROM_DAILY <- STOCK != "VLO" # TRUE: the monthly return to explain is compounded from the stock's daily returns (column 2 of
                               #   DATA_FILE is ignored), the own-return variables "StockReturns -k" and "AVGRETk (-j)" are rebuilt
                               #   from this stock's returns, and "Beta" columns (VLO-specific) are dropped. So one monthly data file serves all.
# History test: ignore a stock's returns before a month, as if it had listed then (the market variables keep their full
# history, exactly like a stock that listed late). Results go to a separate folder ending "_from<month>".
DATA_START <- c()              # e.g. c(VLO = "2012-04") = VLO with the same history as PSX; c() = full history for every stock
RUN_TAG    <- ""          # optional label added to every output folder, e.g. "seed2"
ds_of <- function(s) if (length(DATA_START) && s %in% names(DATA_START) && !is.na(DATA_START[[s]])) as.Date(paste0(DATA_START[[s]], "-01")) else as.Date(NA)
DS <- ds_of(STOCK)
out_dir_for <- function(s) file.path(RESULTS_DIR, paste0("MeanReversion_Results_v3", if (s != "VLO") paste0("_", s) else "",
                                                                          if (nzchar(RUN_TAG)) paste0("_", RUN_TAG) else "",
                                                                          if (!is.na(ds_of(s))) paste0("_from", format(ds_of(s), "%Y-%m")) else ""))
OUT_DIR  <- out_dir_for(STOCK)
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
N_CORES  <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L)

# ---- optimiser budget ----------------------------------------------------------------
INFEAS <- -1000           # objective for infeasible parameters (fix 2): always below any real OOS R2
POLISH_ROUNDS <- 0   # local polish passes after SPSA (fix 4); 0 = off
# Score weights used in the variable score (calibrated monthly). Available: c("a","b","c","d","e","f","g").
#   a = significance (p-value), d = stability of R2, f = per-variable out-of-sample R2
WEIGHTS <- c("a", "d", "f")
# How the p-value enters term a (and c):
#   "loglog" = log(1 + (-log p)): every p-value keeps a distinct value, smaller p scores higher, no explosion near p = 0
#   "raw"    = -log(p): the original term (up to ~690 near p = 0)
#   "rank"   = each month's percentile rank of -log(p) across all variables (0-1)
P_TRANSFORM <- "loglog"
# Weight mode: "simplex" = weights are non-negative shares that sum to 1 (no sign flips, no scale drift);
#              "free"    = unconstrained weights (old behaviour, can be negative and drift in size)
WEIGHT_MODE <- "simplex"
# Economic core: variables ALWAYS in the regression (exact column names in DATA_FILE). They count towards n; the selection
# fills the remaining slots as usual (Corr_t / VIF checked against them). A forced variable is skipped in a month where it is
# missing or has too little history in the training window. character(0) = no forced variables.
FORCE_VARS <- character(0)   # e.g. c("MOCHNG crck"): monthly change of the crack spread, the most stable driver in the data
# Reward steady strength over recent, noisy strength in the variable ranking (both use months up to the end of training only):
SCORE_AVG_MONTHS <- 1   # rank variables by their score AVERAGED over the last SCORE_AVG_MONTHS months (1 = this month only, as before);
                          #   e.g. 12: a variable must have scored well for a year, not just in the latest window
SIGN_MIN <- 0   # a candidate is dropped unless its coefficient had the same sign as now in at least this share of the last
                          #   SIGN_MONTHS months (0 = off; e.g. 0.8). Removes variables whose relationship keeps flipping
SIGN_MONTHS <- 24
P_MAX <- 1   # a candidate is dropped unless its own one-variable regression on VLO (over Regr_Win months, ending at the
                          #   end of the training window) has p-value < P_MAX (1 = off; e.g. 0.1). Forced variables are exempt.
                          #   Months where fewer than n candidates pass simply use fewer variables.
# Parameters held FIXED (not calibrated). Remove an entry to let the optimiser calibrate it again.
FIXED_PARAMS <- list()
POLISH_PARAMS <- c("n", "Corr_t", "Regr_Win", "Z_Win", "Train_MO", "Test_MO", WEIGHTS)   # fixed ones are skipped automatically
# Multi-window calibration objective: each parameter set is scored by its OOS R2 averaged over OBJ_WINDOWS
# consecutive, non-overlapping past test windows (each with its own training window before it).
# 1 = single window (old behaviour). Rewards parameters that keep working across periods (less winner's curse).
OBJ_WINDOWS       <- 1   # with VALIDATION_MODE the 12-month validation does this job more directly
OBJ_RECENT_WEIGHT <- 1    # weight of the most recent window relative to the older ones (1 = equal, 2 = counts double)
# Validation ("future") stage: train -> 24-month test (calibration) -> VAL_WIN-month validation -> trade month.
# Four strategies run side by side: Baseline (test-window winner), (a) choose the candidate that holds up best on
# validation, (b) trade the winner only if its validation OOS R2 > VAL_GATE, (c) choose + gate.
# The trade-month residual uses the validated parameters with variables / coefficients re-estimated on the training
# window just before the validation window. All stages end at or before the trade month (no lookahead).
VALIDATION_MODE <- TRUE   # strategies reported: Baseline, (a) choose, (b) gate, (c) choose + gate,
                          # (d) switch = (a) when the winner's validation OOS R2 < 0, Baseline when it is >= 0
# ---- diagnostics: collinearity, heteroskedasticity, linearity --------------------
VIF_MAX        <- 5           # a variable is added only if its VIF against the ones already chosen is <= VIF_MAX (Inf = off)
HETERO_DIAG    <- TRUE        # each month: Breusch-Pagan test (training window) + variance ratio (test / training residuals)
TRANSFORM_MODE <- "report"   # "none"; "report" = rolling linearity check of the model used each month (report only, trades unchanged);
                              # "adaptive" = the check is USED: each month, a selected variable whose signed log / signed sqrt raises
                              #              the model's adjusted R2 by >= LIN_GAIN on the training window enters in that form
                              #              (decided on training data only; applies to calibration, validation and trades)
                              # "candidates" = signed-log and signed-sqrt versions added as extra candidate variables (check still runs)
LIN_P    <- 0.05              # rolling check: significance level; the per-variable x^2 test uses LIN_P / (number of variables)
LIN_GAIN <- 0.02              # rolling check: a transform counts as better when it raises the model's adjusted R2 by >= LIN_GAIN
# ---- Markov states (binary, from the variance ratio and the OOS R2 of the model behind each trade) -----
MARKOV_MODE <- TRUE   # fit the Markov regime model each month; Baseline, Markov skip and Markov flip are reported side by side
MK_METHOD   <- "hmm3b"   # "hmm3b" = 3-state Markov model on VLO's return deviation (this month vs the past MK_DEV_MONTHS),
                           #           the variance ratio and the average slope of the validation OOS R2 over MK_B_SLOPE_MONTHS;
                           #           states named by variance ratio: low / mid / high; MK_BAD_REGIME_B is state 0
                           # "hmm3" = 3-state Markov model on variance ratio, VLO volatility and the slope of the validation OOS R2;
                           #          the state whose past CLOSED trades did worst is state 0 (skipped / flipped)
                           # "threshold" = state 0 when this month's combined score is below the MK_QUANTILE of its own history
                           #               (fast: reacts every month); "hmm" = 2-state Markov model on the score (slow, persistent regimes)
MK_QUANTILE <- 0.5       # threshold method: quantile of the score's history below which the state is 0 (0.5 = median, 1/3 = lowest third)
MK_ENTER    <- 0.6       # hmm method: switch to state 0 ("bad") when P(bad) > MK_ENTER ...
MK_EXIT     <- 0.4       # ... and back to state 1 only when P(bad) < MK_EXIT (hysteresis)
MK_MIN_HIST <- 12   # months of inputs needed before the Markov model is used (state 1 before that)
MK_ITERS    <- 50        # EM iterations per monthly fit
MK_HIST_WIN <- 100   # months of history the state is judged against (Inf = all history so far; e.g. 120 = last 10 years)
MK_VOL_MONTHS   <- 3     # hmm3: VLO realised volatility over the last 3 months (daily returns up to the decision month's close)
MK_SLOPE_MONTHS <- 6     # hmm3: slope of the validation OOS R2 over the last 6 months (improving vs deteriorating model)
MK_MIN_TRADES   <- 8     # hmm3: a state is ranked only once it has at least 8 closed trades; until 2 states qualify, everything trades
MK_BAD_REGIME   <- "calm" # hmm3: which regime is state 0. "calm" / "normal" / "turbulent" (or several, e.g. c("calm", "turbulent")) =
                          #       fixed in advance (calm = low volatility was the weak regime in every run so far);
                          #       "learned" = the regime whose past closed trades did worst (reacts to noise: not recommended)
MK_INPUT1 <- "retdev"   # hmm3b: first Markov input
                          #   "reversion" = reversion efficacy: correlation between the model's residual at each of the last
                          #                 MK_DEV_MONTHS signals and VLO's return in the FOLLOWING month (only signals whose next
                          #                 month is already over). Negative = mispricings closed (mean reversion works);
                          #                 near 0 / positive = they persisted (the regime where flipping pays)
                          #   "retdev"    = VLO's return this month vs the past MK_DEV_MONTHS months (z-score; previous input)
MK_DEV_MONTHS     <- 24   # hmm3b: window of the first input (signals for "reversion", months for "retdev")
MK_B_SLOPE_MONTHS <- 24   # hmm3b: slope of the validation OOS R2 over the last 24 months
MK_BAD_REGIME_B   <- "low" # hmm3b: state 0 regime(s): "low" / "mid" / "high" variance ratio (or "learned")
# hmm3b "graded" rule: the 3-state model is fitted with each input window below (return deviation and R2 slope);
#   FLIP  if at least MK_FLIP_VOTES fits say "low" (and, if MK_USE_CALM, volatility is calm);
#   SKIP  if at least MK_SKIP_VOTES fits say "low" (or, if MK_USE_CALM, volatility is calm) but the flip condition fails;
#   TRADE otherwise.
MK_ENS_WINDOWS <- c(12, 24, 36)  # input windows of the ensemble fits (months)
MK_FLIP_VOTES  <- 1   # fits (of length(MK_ENS_WINDOWS)) that must say "low" to flip; 2 of 3 = majority
MK_SKIP_VOTES  <- Inf            # fits that must say "low" to skip when not flipping (Inf = never skip; e.g. 1)
MK_USE_CALM    <- FALSE          # TRUE = flipping also requires calm volatility, and calm alone skips
                                 #   (calm months were profitable before 2020 in the latest run, so off by default)
MK_CALM_Q      <- 1/3            # calm = VLO's MK_VOL_MONTHS-month volatility in the lowest third of its own history up to the month
MK_BAD_BELOW    <- 0     # hmm3, "learned" only: the worst regime becomes state 0 only if its closed trades averaged BELOW this;
                         #       if every regime is profitable, nothing is skipped or flipped
VAL_WIN         <- 12
# ---- combined model: one validation strategy + one Markov rule, reported as the headline result -------------
COMBINED_STRATEGY <- "base"   # "base", "a", "b", "c" or "d". Validation now only feeds the Markov state (R2 slope);
                             # the validation strategies are still reported in the grid for reference
COMBINED_MARKOV   <- "graded"   # "none", "skip", "flip" or "graded" (ensemble + calm volatility, see MK_ENS_WINDOWS)
VAL_GATE        <- 0
if (QUICK_MODE) {
  CAL <- list(starts = 2, iters = 15, n_pert = 1); TRAIN_WIN_STEP <- 12; TEST_WIN_STEP <- 8; WINDOW_SCORE_MONTHS <- 6
  POLISH_ROUNDS <- min(POLISH_ROUNDS, 2); WINDOW_TOP_K <- min(WINDOW_TOP_K, 2)
} else {
  CAL <- list(starts = 6, iters = 60, n_pert = 2)
}
CHECKPOINT_EVERY <- 12
NAG_MU <- 0.8; NAG_A0 <- 0.25; NAG_C0 <- 0.15; NAG_VMAX <- 1.0
MEMO_CAP <- list(reg = 60, zreg = 120, oos = 60, zoos = 150)
stopifnot("SMOOTHING must be 'average' or 'none'" = SMOOTHING %in% c("average", "none"))
LAYER2 <- SMOOTHING == "average"
# ---- calibration ranges: built-in defaults, then the parameter table ----
PARAM_MIN <- c(Regr_Win = 5, Z_Win = 3, Train_MO = 5, Test_MO = 2)
N_RANGE <- c(5, 8); TRAIN_WIN_RANGE <- c(60, 120); TEST_WIN_RANGE <- c(24, 24)
# ---- calibration ranges from the parameter table ----
trow <- function(nm) { r <- SMOOTH_TABLE[trimws(SMOOTH_TABLE$name) == nm, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(r) || !all(c("min", "max") %in% names(r))) c(NA_real_, NA_real_) else as.numeric(unlist(r[1, c("min", "max")])) }
PARAM_MAX <- c(Regr_Win = Inf, Z_Win = Inf, Train_MO = Inf, Test_MO = Inf)
for (p in names(PARAM_MAX)) { r <- trow(p); if (!is.na(r[1])) PARAM_MIN[p] <- r[1]; if (!is.na(r[2])) PARAM_MAX[p] <- r[2] }
r <- trow("n");         if (!is.na(r[1])) N_RANGE[1] <- r[1];         if (!is.na(r[2])) N_RANGE[2] <- r[2]
r <- trow("Train_Win"); if (!is.na(r[1])) TRAIN_WIN_RANGE[1] <- r[1]; if (!is.na(r[2])) TRAIN_WIN_RANGE[2] <- r[2]
r <- trow("Test_Win");  if (!is.na(r[1])) TEST_WIN_RANGE[1] <- r[1];  if (!is.na(r[2])) TEST_WIN_RANGE[2] <- r[2]
r <- trow("Min_Res");   MINRES_GRID <- MINRES_GRID[MINRES_GRID >= (if (is.na(r[1])) -Inf else r[1] - 1e-9) & MINRES_GRID <= (if (is.na(r[2])) Inf else r[2] + 1e-9)]
if (!length(MINRES_GRID)) stop("Parameter table: the Min_Res range leaves no value of the Min_Res grid (0, 0.05, ..., 0.60)")
DEFAULT_TRADE_RULES["min_res"] <- min(max(DEFAULT_TRADE_RULES[["min_res"]], min(MINRES_GRID)), max(MINRES_GRID))
CORR_RANGE <- { r <- trow("Corr_t"); c(if (is.na(r[1])) 0 else r[1], if (is.na(r[2])) 1 else r[2]) }
W_RANGE <- t(vapply(letters[1:7], function(w) { r <- trow(w); c(if (is.na(r[1])) 0 else r[1], if (is.na(r[2])) 1 else r[2]) }, c(0, 0)))
stopifnot("Parameter table: a min is above its max" = all(PARAM_MIN[names(PARAM_MAX)] <= PARAM_MAX) && N_RANGE[1] <= N_RANGE[2] &&
            CORR_RANGE[1] <= CORR_RANGE[2] && all(W_RANGE[, 1] <= W_RANGE[, 2]))
stopifnot("WINDOW_UPDATE must be 'monthly' or 'january'" = WINDOW_UPDATE %in% c("monthly", "january"),
          "WINDOW_TOP_K must be >= 1" = WINDOW_TOP_K >= 1)
# Minimum windows follow from the ratio rules, so every window pair can hold at least N_RANGE[1] variables
# (n >= 5 -> Train_Win >= 60, Test_Win >= 40). Without this, short pairs would force n below the minimum.
TRAIN_WIN_RANGE[1] <- max(TRAIN_WIN_RANGE[1], TRAIN_PER_VAR * if (identical(COMBINE_VARS, "univariate")) 1 else N_RANGE[1])
# Univariate combination: the number of variables is calibrated (a fixed n would make the univariate n-range pointless).
# Set UNIVARIATE_FIX_N <- TRUE to keep n from FIXED_PARAMS anyway. The other FIXED_PARAMS stay fixed either way.
if (identical(COMBINE_VARS, "univariate") && "n" %in% names(FIXED_PARAMS) && !isTRUE(get0("UNIVARIATE_FIX_N"))) {
  FIXED_PARAMS$n <- NULL
  message("COMBINE_VARS = \"univariate\": n removed from FIXED_PARAMS and calibrated within N_RANGE = ", paste(N_RANGE, collapse = "-"))
}
TEST_WIN_RANGE[1]  <- max(TEST_WIN_RANGE[1],  TEST_PER_VAR  * N_RANGE[1])
stopifnot("Window ranges too short for the minimum number of variables" =
            TRAIN_WIN_RANGE[1] <= TRAIN_WIN_RANGE[2] && TEST_WIN_RANGE[1] <= TEST_WIN_RANGE[2])
```

# 2. Data

```{r load-data}
parse_ym <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, c("Date", "POSIXct", "POSIXt"))) return(as.Date(format(as.Date(x), "%Y-%m-01")))
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(as.Date(format(as.Date(x, origin = "1899-12-30"), "%Y-%m-01")))
  mm <- regmatches(as.character(x), regexec("(\\d{4})\\s*[-/.]\\s*(\\d{1,2})", as.character(x)))
  y <- as.integer(vapply(mm, function(v) if (length(v) == 3) v[2] else NA_character_, ""))
  mo <- as.integer(vapply(mm, function(v) if (length(v) == 3) v[3] else NA_character_, ""))
  as.Date(ifelse(is.na(y), NA, sprintf("%04d-%02d-01", y, mo)))
}
parse_num <- function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(as.numeric(x))
  s <- trimws(as.character(x)); pct <- grepl("%", s)
  v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("[%,\\s]", "", s))); ifelse(pct, v / 100, v)
}
raw_m <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(DATA_DIR, DATA_FILE), sheet = 1)
dts <- parse_ym(raw_m[[1]]); stopifnot("Could not parse the Y/Mo column" = all(!is.na(dts)))
o <- order(dts)
MON <- list(dates = dts[o], y = parse_num(raw_m[[2]])[o],
            X = as.matrix(as.data.frame(lapply(raw_m[-(1:2)], parse_num)))[o, , drop = FALSE])
colnames(MON$X) <- names(raw_m)[-(1:2)]
MON$X <- MON$X[, colSums(!is.na(MON$X)) > 0, drop = FALSE]

  raw_d <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(DATA_DIR, PEER_FILE), sheet = "DailyChanges", guess_max = 1e6)   # columns start blank before listing
  if (!PEER_COLS[[STOCK]] %in% names(raw_d)) stop(sprintf("Column '%s' (for %s) not found in %s", PEER_COLS[[STOCK]], STOCK, PEER_FILE))
  DAY <- data.frame(Date = as.Date(raw_d[[1]]), r = parse_num(raw_d[[PEER_COLS[[STOCK]]]]))
  if (sum(is.finite(DAY$r)) < 250) stop(sprintf("%s: fewer than 250 daily returns read from %s", STOCK, PEER_FILE))
} else {
  raw_d <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(DATA_DIR, DAILY_FILE), sheet = 1)
  DAY <- data.frame(Date = as.Date(raw_d[[1]]), r = parse_num(raw_d[[2]]))
}
DAY <- DAY[!is.na(DAY$Date), ]; DAY <- DAY[order(DAY$Date), ]
lagv <- function(x, k) if (k == 0) x else c(rep(NA_real_, k), head(x, -k))
rebuild_own <- function(X, y) {          # own-return variables from the stock's monthly returns y
  cn <- colnames(X)
  for (j in grep("^StockReturns\\s*-\\s*\\d+$", cn)) X[, j] <- lagv(y, as.integer(sub("^.*-\\s*", "", cn[j])))
  for (j in grep("^AVGRET\\d+(\\s*-\\s*\\d+)?$", cn)) {          # AVGRETw = mean of the previous w months (current excluded)
    w <- as.integer(sub("^AVGRET(\\d+).*$", "\\1", cn[j])); k <- if (grepl("-", cn[j])) as.integer(sub("^.*-\\s*", "", cn[j])) else 0L
    base <- vapply(seq_along(y), function(t) if (t <= w) NA_real_ else mean(y[(t - w):(t - 1)]), 0)
    X[, j] <- lagv(base, k)
  }
  X
}
if (Y_FROM_DAILY) {                     # monthly return of STOCK from its daily returns (months with < 10 daily returns -> missing)
  ymd <- format(DAY$Date, "%Y-%m")
  my <- tapply(DAY$r, ymd, function(r) if (sum(is.finite(r)) >= 10) prod(1 + r[is.finite(r)]) - 1 else NA_real_)
  MON$y <- as.numeric(my[format(MON$dates, "%Y-%m")])

  dropb <- grep("^Beta", cn); if (length(dropb)) MON$X <- MON$X[, -dropb, drop = FALSE]
  message(sprintf("%s: monthly returns from %s (%d months); own-return variables rebuilt; %d Beta columns dropped",
                  STOCK, DAILY_FILE, sum(is.finite(MON$y)), length(dropb)))
}
if (!is.na(DS)) {                       # history test: the stock's returns before DS are treated as not existing
  MON$y[MON$dates < DS] <- NA

  for (j in grep("^(StockReturns\\s*-\\s*\\d+|AVGRET\\d+(\\s*-\\s*\\d+)?)$", colnames(Xr))) MON$X[is.na(Xr[, j]), j] <- NA   # returns before DS
  jb <- grep("^Beta", colnames(MON$X)); if (length(jb)) MON$X[MON$dates < DS, jb] <- NA
```
